title: `_new_ingress_rule` cyclomatic complexity 27 (54 lines)
detail: `_new_ingress_rule` (lines 106–178) has CCN=27 across 54 lines. Functions this complex require an exponential number of test cases to cover all paths and are a defect magnet. Fix: extract well-named helpers for each major decision cluster.

title: Line 86: broad `except Exception` (BLE001)
detail: Catching `Exception` at line 86 prevents distinguishing expected errors from unexpected failures. Fix: catch specific exception types, or re-raise after logging if a broad catch is intentional.

title: verbose exception re-raise at line 380
detail: `raise exc` replaces the original exception losing the traceback. Use bare `raise` inside `except` to re-raise with the full chain preserved.

title: 2× broad `except Exception` (W0703) — lines 645, 701
detail: 2 broad `except Exception` clauses (first at line 645). Each swallows unexpected error types. Fix: catch specific exceptions at each site.

title: 3× exception raised without `from` in except block (W0707, first at line 87)
detail: At 3 location(s) (first at line 87), a new exception is raised inside an `except` block without `raise ... from original_exc`. This discards the original traceback and makes debugging harder. Fix: `raise NewExc(...) from exc` to preserve the chain.

title: 2× too-many-branches (R0912) — function(s) at lines 106, 587
detail: 2 functions have more branches than pylint's threshold. High branch count multiplies test cases needed for coverage and makes the function a defect magnet. Fix: extract decision clusters into named helper functions.

title: Builtins `id`, `list` shadowed by local variable (W0622)
detail: Local variable(s) at lines 47, 293, 307, 357, 443 shadow the builtin(s) id, list. If the builtin is needed elsewhere in the same scope, the shadowing causes a confusing `TypeError` or silent misbehavior. Fix: rename the local variable to avoid shadowing.

title: unused variable assignment (W0612, line 436)
detail: Variable assigned at line 436 is never used. Dead assignments may indicate a forgotten use. Fix: remove the assignment or prefix with `_`.
